newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy seen selling marks for lira - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy seen selling marks for lira - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Italy sold marks for lire at around 998.50 per mark as the Italian currency headed towards the 1,000 per mark barrier, dealers said.
The lira was quoted at 999.10/9.60 per mark at 1542 GMT, at the day's low and a fraction away from the 1,000 per mark barrier.
It has not breached the barrier since November 22, 1996, shortly before it rejoined Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
"We saw intervention at 998.50," one Italian dealer said.

Others said they had heard talk of intervention all day and earlier traders reported the central bank had been checking lira rates against the dollar at about 1,688 and against the mark at around 998.
While one said he seen nothing concrete he believed the central bank had been trying to stem speculation on the lira all day. "But it (mark/lira) is still going up," he added.

The lira has come under pressure recently over concerns about the prospects for Europe's planned economic and monetary union. Shortly after the intervention news, the currency fell through the psychological 1,000 per mark barrier to 1,001.50, its lowest level since November 20, 1996.
Dealers said a clean break at 1,000 would propel the currency back towards 1,005.
The lira returned to Europe's exchange rate mechanism late last year and began trading in the ERM on November 25 with a central parity against the mark of 990.
